sentences.text: 7. Issue notice.
Mr. Sanjay Lao, learned Standing Counsel accepts notice on behalf of the State.

8. All the petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr.
Siddharth and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Durga Prasad from Police Station Rajouri Garden, Delhi.
9. Brief facts of the present case are that petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 were married on 17.04.2016 as per Sikh Rites and Ceremonies at New Delhi.

Due to some temperamental differences,
the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 were not able to live together and have been living separately since 16.12.2017.
The respondent no. 2 lodged a complaint with CAW Cell (West).

The said complaint culminated into registration of an FIR bearing no. 202/2019 at Police Station Rajouri Garden, Delhi, for the offences punishable under Section 498a/406/34 of IPC against petitioners.
It is stated that both the parties have amicably settled the matter.

10. On a query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent No.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties.

11. It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 14:20:06 items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family members.
12. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the settled amount from petitioner no. 1 and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

13. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

14. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 202/2019 registered at Police Station Rajouri Garden, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
